text: This is Dave, 29, and behind. Behind what? The list on his fridge, written at 18. By my own company, a house, front row at Thunderwolf. 11 months left, ticks, zero. Tonight's scroll, an engagement, new house keys, a classmate's startup. So is Dave behind, whose schedule says so? Suspect one, Silicon Valley, Mark Zuckerberg. Young people are just smarter. He said it at 22. In 2020, economists Pierre Azoulay and Benjamin Jones checked 2.7 million American founders. The fastest-growing one in a thousand, average founder age, 45. A 50-year-old was 1.8 times as likely to get there as a 30-year-old. Item one isn't late. It's 15 years early. Suspect two, the feed. Dave follows 30 founders under 30 for motivation. In 2016, Todd Rogers and Avi Feller followed nearly 6,000 online students, grading three random classmates' essays. Graded average essays, 68% passed. Graded the very best, 45. The best essays didn't teach them to write. They taught them to quit. Dave's feed is all best essays. Now, check the handwriting. Suspect three, wrote the list. Aged 18. In 2013, Daniel Gilbert's team asked over 19,000 people, aged 18 to 68, How much did you change in the last 10 years? A lot. In the next 10, not much. At every age. Everyone thinks they're finished. 18-year-old Dave was sure he'd love Thunderwolf forever. He hasn't played them since 2016. Dave isn't behind. He's taking orders, from an 18-year-old. Tonight, write your own list. No dates. Only what you still want. Dave kept his list. He crossed out by 30, and Thunderwolf. You are not behind. You're just not 18 anymore.
